title: Energy storage assembly with heating film
abstract: A energy storage assembly is disclosed that includes a resistive heating film attached to the pack underside. In some embodiments the energy storage assembly further includes a module housing with forced-air cooling ducts between cell rows and a sealed pack enclosure with a pressure-equalising membrane. The arrangement lowers parasitic cooling power.
claims: 1. A energy storage assembly comprising: a resistive heating film attached to the pack underside; a module housing with forced-air cooling ducts between cell rows; and a sealed pack enclosure with a pressure-equalising membrane.
2. The energy storage assembly of claim 1, further comprising a pyrolytic graphite sheet conducting heat toward a side wall.
3. The energy storage assembly of claim 2, further comprising a fan whose duty cycle follows the highest measured cell temperature.

title: Protective coating system with hydrophobic topcoat
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a protective coating system. The protective coating system comprises a self-healing polymer containing reversible hydrogen bonds without any capsules and a fluorinated topcoat repelling water. Additionally, a non-contact eddy current gauge for measuring film thickness is provided. This improves adhesion on steel.
claims: 1. A protective coating system comprising: a self-healing polymer containing reversible hydrogen bonds without any capsules; a fluorinated topcoat repelling water; and a non-contact eddy current gauge for measuring film thickness.
2. The protective coating system of claim 1, further comprising an electroless nickel-phosphorus plating.

title: Coated article with low-solvent binder
abstract: A coated article is disclosed that includes curing by ultraviolet light-emitting diodes to a dry film thickness of 80 to 120 micrometres. In some embodiments the coated article further includes a silane adhesion promoter applied to a grit-blasted surface and microcapsules containing a corrosion inhibitor that release when a crack forms in the coating. The arrangement reduces maintenance repainting.
claims: 1. A coated article comprising: curing by ultraviolet light-emitting diodes to a dry film thickness of 80 to 120 micrometres; a silane adhesion promoter applied to a grit-blasted surface; and microcapsules containing a corrosion inhibitor that release when a crack forms in the coating.
2. The coated article of claim 1, further comprising graphene oxide platelets aligned parallel to the surface within an epoxy matrix.
3. The coated article of claim 2, further comprising an undercoat loaded with zinc dust protecting the steel galvanically.
4. The coated article of claim 3, further comprising a water-borne acrylic dispersion with reduced solvent content.

title: Coated article with powder coating and carbon film
abstract: Embodiments of a coated article are described, characterised by a thermosetting polyester powder applied electrostatically. Variants include an intumescent paint layer that swells when exposed to heat. The design improves adhesion on steel while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A coated article comprising: a thermosetting polyester powder applied electrostatically; a diamond-like carbon film deposited by physical vapour deposition; and an intumescent paint layer that swells when exposed to heat.
2. The coated article of claim 1, further comprising a fluorinated topcoat repelling water.

title: Protective coating system with low-solvent binder and shielding paint
abstract: A protective coating system is disclosed that includes a water-borne acrylic dispersion with reduced solvent content. In some embodiments the protective coating system further includes a silver-filled conductive coating for electromagnetic shielding and a chromium-free conversion pretreatment of an aluminium substrate. The arrangement extends service life in marine environments.
claims: 1. A protective coating system comprising: a water-borne acrylic dispersion with reduced solvent content; a silver-filled conductive coating for electromagnetic shielding; and a chromium-free conversion pretreatment of an aluminium substrate.
2. The protective coating system of claim 1, further comprising an intumescent paint layer that swells when exposed to heat.
3. The protective coating system of claim 2, further comprising ceramic particles dispersed in a polyurethane binder for abrasion resistance.

title: Powder bed fusion system with orientation planning and distortion simulation
abstract: A powder bed fusion system is disclosed that includes an orientation planner minimising overhang area. In some embodiments the powder bed fusion system further includes a thermal distortion simulation used to pre-compensate part geometry and an abrasive flow process polishing internal channels. The arrangement shortens qualification time.
claims: 1. A powder bed fusion system comprising: an orientation planner minimising overhang area; a thermal distortion simulation used to pre-compensate part geometry; and an abrasive flow process polishing internal channels.
2. The powder bed fusion system of claim 1, further comprising a binder jetting printhead depositing a binder on a powder layer.
3. The powder bed fusion system of claim 2, further comprising a post-build stress-relief heat treatment.

title: Battery module with heat spreader foils and fan control
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a battery module. The battery module comprises an insulated shipping container for batteries and an aluminium heat-spreading foil wrapped around each cylindrical cell. Additionally, a fan whose duty cycle follows the highest measured cell temperature is provided. This reduces temperature spread between cells.
claims: 1. A battery module comprising: an insulated shipping container for batteries; an aluminium heat-spreading foil wrapped around each cylindrical cell; and a fan whose duty cycle follows the highest measured cell temperature.
2. The battery module of claim 1, further comprising a pyrolytic graphite sheet conducting heat toward a side wall.

title: Powder bed fusion system with powder recycling and orientation planning
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a powder bed fusion system. The powder bed fusion system comprises a sieving station returning unfused powder to the hopper and an orientation planner minimising overhang area. Additionally, a binder jetting printhead depositing a binder on a powder layer is provided. This lowers scrap rate.
claims: 1. A powder bed fusion system comprising: a sieving station returning unfused powder to the hopper; an orientation planner minimising overhang area; and a binder jetting printhead depositing a binder on a powder layer.
2. The powder bed fusion system of claim 1, further comprising a wire-fed arc deposition head mounted on a robot arm.

title: Condition monitoring device with proximity sensing
abstract: A condition monitoring device is disclosed that includes a cloud-based fault analysis service receiving raw waveforms. In some embodiments the condition monitoring device further includes an inductive proximity sensor detecting a rotating target and an electrochemical gas detection cell with a replaceable filter. The arrangement shortens fault detection latency.
claims: 1. A condition monitoring device comprising: a cloud-based fault analysis service receiving raw waveforms; an inductive proximity sensor detecting a rotating target; and an electrochemical gas detection cell with a replaceable filter.
2. The condition monitoring device of claim 1, further comprising a diaphragm pressure transmitter with a current loop output.

title: Energy storage assembly with air-cooled housing and derated charging
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a energy storage assembly. The energy storage assembly comprises a module housing with forced-air cooling ducts between cell rows and a charging profile that derates current as cell temperature increases. Additionally, an aluminium heat-spreading foil wrapped around each cylindrical cell is provided. This extends cycle life.
claims: 1. A energy storage assembly comprising: a module housing with forced-air cooling ducts between cell rows; a charging profile that derates current as cell temperature increases; and an aluminium heat-spreading foil wrapped around each cylindrical cell.
2. The energy storage assembly of claim 1, further comprising a busbar with an integrated heat sink.

title: Additive manufacturing apparatus with scan strategy
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a additive manufacturing apparatus. The additive manufacturing apparatus comprises a stripe scan strategy rotated by sixty-seven degrees between layers and hot isostatic pressing to close internal pores. Additionally, a binder jetting printhead depositing a binder on a powder layer is provided. This lowers scrap rate.
claims: 1. A additive manufacturing apparatus comprising: a stripe scan strategy rotated by sixty-seven degrees between layers; hot isostatic pressing to close internal pores; and a binder jetting printhead depositing a binder on a powder layer.

title: Corrosion protection scheme with chromium-free pretreatment
abstract: Embodiments of a corrosion protection scheme are described, characterised by a chromium-free conversion pretreatment of an aluminium substrate. Variants include a water-borne acrylic dispersion with reduced solvent content. The design improves adhesion on steel while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A corrosion protection scheme comprising: a chromium-free conversion pretreatment of an aluminium substrate; a diamond-like carbon film deposited by physical vapour deposition; and a water-borne acrylic dispersion with reduced solvent content.
2. The corrosion protection scheme of claim 1, further comprising a non-contact eddy current gauge for measuring film thickness.

title: Condition monitoring device with thermocouple assembly
abstract: Embodiments of a condition monitoring device are described, characterised by a calibration routine storing correction coefficients in non-volatile memory. Variants include an ultrasonic transducer pair measuring transit time through the pipe wall. The design shortens fault detection latency while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A condition monitoring device comprising: a calibration routine storing correction coefficients in non-volatile memory; an underwater microphone fixed to the conduit sensing hiss produced by a breach; and an ultrasonic transducer pair measuring transit time through the pipe wall.
2. The condition monitoring device of claim 1, further comprising a mineral-insulated thermocouple with a thermowell.
3. The condition monitoring device of claim 2, further comprising an overnight recording period used because demand-related noise is minimal.
4. The condition monitoring device of claim 3, further comprising a time-delay comparison between a pair of detectors to determine where along the line the leak is.

title: Corrosion protection scheme with low-solvent binder
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a corrosion protection scheme. The corrosion protection scheme comprises a water-borne acrylic dispersion with reduced solvent content and a non-contact eddy current gauge for measuring film thickness. Additionally, an intumescent paint layer that swells when exposed to heat is provided. This extends service life in marine environments.
claims: 1. A corrosion protection scheme comprising: a water-borne acrylic dispersion with reduced solvent content; a non-contact eddy current gauge for measuring film thickness; and an intumescent paint layer that swells when exposed to heat.
2. The corrosion protection scheme of claim 1, further comprising a thermosetting polyester powder applied electrostatically.

title: Thermal management system with graphite sheet and derated charging
abstract: A thermal management system is disclosed that includes a pyrolytic graphite sheet conducting heat toward a side wall. In some embodiments the thermal management system further includes a charging profile that derates current as cell temperature increases and a heat pipe transferring heat from the module core to a condenser section. The arrangement lowers parasitic cooling power.
claims: 1. A thermal management system comprising: a pyrolytic graphite sheet conducting heat toward a side wall; a charging profile that derates current as cell temperature increases; and a heat pipe transferring heat from the module core to a condenser section.
2. The thermal management system of claim 1, further comprising an aluminium heat-spreading foil wrapped around each cylindrical cell.

title: Corrosion protection scheme with hydrophobic topcoat
abstract: A corrosion protection scheme is disclosed that includes a fluorinated topcoat repelling water. In some embodiments the corrosion protection scheme further includes a water-borne acrylic dispersion with reduced solvent content and an electroless nickel-phosphorus plating. The arrangement extends service life in marine environments.
claims: 1. A corrosion protection scheme comprising: a fluorinated topcoat repelling water; a water-borne acrylic dispersion with reduced solvent content; and an electroless nickel-phosphorus plating.
2. The corrosion protection scheme of claim 1, further comprising a sealed anodic oxide layer on an aluminium alloy.

title: Battery pack with cell balancing (continuation)
abstract: A battery pack is disclosed that has a bypass circuit that isolates a failing cell group without interrupting current to the load. In certain embodiments the battery pack further includes a bench that characterises residual capacity and resistance of every used cell using a fixed current-pulse routine and an automated gripping tool extracting cells from the donor pack intact. The arrangement lowers temperature spread between cells.
claims: 1. A battery pack comprising: a bypass circuit that isolates a failing cell group without interrupting current to the load; a bench that characterises residual capacity and resistance of every used cell using a fixed current-pulse routine; and an automated gripping tool extracting cells from the donor pack intact.
2. The battery pack of claim 1, further comprising a digital passport stored on each module recording its usage history and test results.
3. The battery pack of claim 2, further comprising an unsupervised sorting routine assembling cells with similar characteristics into batches using the characterised values.

title: Sensor node with proximity sensing
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sensor node. The sensor node comprises a piezo ultrasonic pickup on the toolholder sensing high frequency events and a link to the machine controller ordering a replacement of the cutter once the estimate hits a bound. Additionally, a descriptor merging effective load level with energy in frequency bands for every pass is provided. This lowers installation cost.
claims: 1. A sensor node comprising: a piezo ultrasonic pickup on the toolholder sensing high frequency events; a link to the machine controller ordering a replacement of the cutter once the estimate hits a bound; and a descriptor merging effective load level with energy in frequency bands for every pass.
2. The sensor node of claim 1, further comprising a fitted predictor returning the width of flank wear in microns.
3. The sensor node of claim 2, further comprising a current transformer around a drive conductor logging the electric load of the cutting spindle.

title: Battery module with busbar heat sink
abstract: Embodiments of a battery module are described, characterised by a relay network changing the series-parallel topology of cell sets while in use. Variants include a shunt path disconnecting a deteriorating cell cluster while the load stays supplied. The design extends cycle life while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A battery module comprising: a relay network changing the series-parallel topology of cell sets while in use; a bench that characterises residual capacity and resistance of every used cell using a fixed current-pulse routine; and a shunt path disconnecting a deteriorating cell cluster while the load stays supplied.
2. The battery module of claim 1, further comprising an unsupervised sorting routine assembling cells with similar characteristics into batches using the characterised values.
3. The battery module of claim 2, further comprising an electronic record kept on every module holding past operating data and measurements.
4. The battery module of claim 3, further comprising a busbar with an integrated heat sink.

title: Sensor node with humidity compensation and long-range gateway
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sensor node. The sensor node comprises a wired resistance thermometer in a laboratory furnace and a humidity compensation step applied to capacitive readings. Additionally, a gateway aggregating readings from field devices over a long-range radio link is provided. This shortens fault detection latency.
claims: 1. A sensor node comprising: a wired resistance thermometer in a laboratory furnace; a humidity compensation step applied to capacitive readings; and a gateway aggregating readings from field devices over a long-range radio link.
2. The sensor node of claim 1, further comprising an electrochemical gas detection cell with a replaceable filter.

title: Battery pack with air-cooled housing and cell balancing
abstract: Embodiments of a battery pack are described, characterised by a balancing circuit that equalises the state of charge of series-connected cells. Variants include a pyrolytic graphite sheet conducting heat toward a side wall. The design reduces temperature spread between cells while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A battery pack comprising: a balancing circuit that equalises the state of charge of series-connected cells; a circuit-based estimator tracking resistance increase using step-current behaviour; and a pyrolytic graphite sheet conducting heat toward a side wall.
2. The battery pack of claim 1, further comprising retained bulge event data within the pack management unit supporting service scheduling.
3. The battery pack of claim 2, further comprising a recharge protocol that throttles current if the bulging velocity passes a ceiling.
4. The battery pack of claim 3, further comprising a module housing with forced-air cooling ducts between cell rows.

title: Energy storage assembly with graphite sheet
abstract: Embodiments of a energy storage assembly are described, characterised by a warm-up timetable matched to the route target and planned departure. Variants include an alternating current excitation at a selected frequency that warms the cell through internal impedance. The design extends cycle life while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A energy storage assembly comprising: a warm-up timetable matched to the route target and planned departure; a resistive metal sheet inside the electrode assembly warmed by the battery's discharge current; and an alternating current excitation at a selected frequency that warms the cell through internal impedance.
2. The energy storage assembly of claim 1, further comprising a lithium plating detector that analyses the voltage plateau during relaxation after charging.
3. The energy storage assembly of claim 2, further comprising a temperature-dependent charge current limit read from a lookup table stored in the controller.
4. The energy storage assembly of claim 3, further comprising a pyrolytic graphite sheet conducting heat toward a side wall.

title: Sensor node with long-range gateway and edge unit
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sensor node. The sensor node comprises a gateway aggregating readings from field devices over a long-range radio link and an edge computing unit forwarding alarms to a supervisory system. Additionally, a fibre Bragg grating strain sensor bonded to the structure is provided. This extends battery life.
claims: 1. A sensor node comprising: a gateway aggregating readings from field devices over a long-range radio link; an edge computing unit forwarding alarms to a supervisory system; and a fibre Bragg grating strain sensor bonded to the structure.
2. The sensor node of claim 1, further comprising a guided-wave radar probe for tank level measurement.

title: Battery module with heat spreader foils
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a battery module. The battery module comprises a fibre optic strain sensor embedded between cells that measures cell swelling and a stored log of expansion incidents in controller memory used to plan servicing. Additionally, a lumped electrical model deriving rising ohmic resistance from the response to current pulses is provided. This lowers parasitic cooling power.
claims: 1. A battery module comprising: a fibre optic strain sensor embedded between cells that measures cell swelling; a stored log of expansion incidents in controller memory used to plan servicing; and a lumped electrical model deriving rising ohmic resistance from the response to current pulses.
2. The battery module of claim 1, further comprising a charging profile that reduces current when the swelling rate exceeds a limit.
3. The battery module of claim 2, further comprising a pressing plate with a motorised clamp load regulated in response to sensed expansion.

title: Corrosion protection scheme with sol-gel layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a corrosion protection scheme. The corrosion protection scheme comprises a tensile bond measurement logged in MPa and a magnetic heating loop raising the pipe to a set temperature prior to coating. Additionally, a yttria-stabilised zirconia layer deposited by plasma spraying is provided. This improves adhesion on steel.
claims: 1. A corrosion protection scheme comprising: a tensile bond measurement logged in MPa; a magnetic heating loop raising the pipe to a set temperature prior to coating; and a yttria-stabilised zirconia layer deposited by plasma spraying.
2. The corrosion protection scheme of claim 1, further comprising a voltage-based flaw finder discovering tiny defects in the layer.
3. The corrosion protection scheme of claim 2, further comprising a sol-gel silica layer applied by dip coating.
4. The corrosion protection scheme of claim 3, further comprising a chromium-free conversion pretreatment of an aluminium substrate.

title: Protective coating system with powder coating and sol-gel layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a protective coating system. The protective coating system comprises a thermosetting polyester powder applied electrostatically and a sol-gel silica layer applied by dip coating. Additionally, a non-contact eddy current gauge for measuring film thickness is provided. This improves adhesion on steel.
claims: 1. A protective coating system comprising: a thermosetting polyester powder applied electrostatically; a sol-gel silica layer applied by dip coating; and a non-contact eddy current gauge for measuring film thickness.

title: Battery pack with heating film
abstract: A battery pack is disclosed that includes a resistive heating film attached to the pack underside. In some embodiments the battery pack further includes a dielectric fluid in which the cells are partially immersed and a fan whose duty cycle follows the highest measured cell temperature. The arrangement improves fast-charging performance.
claims: 1. A battery pack comprising: a resistive heating film attached to the pack underside; a dielectric fluid in which the cells are partially immersed; and a fan whose duty cycle follows the highest measured cell temperature.
2. The battery pack of claim 1, further comprising an aerogel insulation blanket covering the pack lid.

title: Protective coating system with sol-gel layer
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a protective coating system. The protective coating system comprises a sol-gel silica layer applied by dip coating and a non-contact eddy current gauge for measuring film thickness. Additionally, a silver-filled conductive coating for electromagnetic shielding is provided. This extends service life in marine environments.
claims: 1. A protective coating system comprising: a sol-gel silica layer applied by dip coating; a non-contact eddy current gauge for measuring film thickness; and a silver-filled conductive coating for electromagnetic shielding.
2. The protective coating system of claim 1, further comprising a copper-free anti-fouling paint releasing a biocide slowly.

title: Battery pack with immersion cooling
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a battery pack. The battery pack comprises a dielectric fluid in which the cells are partially immersed and an aerogel insulation blanket covering the pack lid. Additionally, a pyrolytic graphite sheet conducting heat toward a side wall is provided. This reduces temperature spread between cells.
claims: 1. A battery pack comprising: a dielectric fluid in which the cells are partially immersed; an aerogel insulation blanket covering the pack lid; and a pyrolytic graphite sheet conducting heat toward a side wall.
2. The battery pack of claim 1, further comprising an aluminium heat-spreading foil wrapped around each cylindrical cell.
3. The battery pack of claim 2, further comprising a fan whose duty cycle follows the highest measured cell temperature.

title: Energy storage assembly with busbar heat sink and heat pipe
abstract: Embodiments of a energy storage assembly are described, characterised by a busbar with an integrated heat sink. Variants include a charging profile that derates current as cell temperature increases. The design reduces temperature spread between cells while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A energy storage assembly comprising: a busbar with an integrated heat sink; a heat pipe transferring heat from the module core to a condenser section; and a charging profile that derates current as cell temperature increases.

title: Powder bed fusion system with wire deposition
abstract: A powder bed fusion system is disclosed that includes a wire-fed arc deposition head mounted on a robot arm. In some embodiments the powder bed fusion system further includes hot isostatic pressing to close internal pores and an abrasive flow process polishing internal channels. The arrangement reduces porosity in finished parts.
claims: 1. A powder bed fusion system comprising: a wire-fed arc deposition head mounted on a robot arm; hot isostatic pressing to close internal pores; and an abrasive flow process polishing internal channels.
2. The powder bed fusion system of claim 1, further comprising a post-build stress-relief heat treatment.
3. The powder bed fusion system of claim 2, further comprising a stripe scan strategy rotated by sixty-seven degrees between layers.

claims: 1. A thermal management system comprising: a module housing with forced-air cooling ducts between cell rows; a dielectric fluid in which the cells are partially immersed; and a resistive heating film attached to the pack underside.
2. The thermal management system of claim 1, further comprising a busbar with an integrated heat sink.

title: Protective coating system with thermal barrier
abstract: A protective coating system is disclosed that includes a pneumatic boot that inflates to crack the ice. In some embodiments the protective coating system further includes a yttria-stabilised zirconia layer deposited by plasma spraying and ceramic particles dispersed in a polyurethane binder for abrasion resistance. The arrangement lowers solvent emissions.
claims: 1. A protective coating system comprising: a pneumatic boot that inflates to crack the ice; a yttria-stabilised zirconia layer deposited by plasma spraying; and ceramic particles dispersed in a polyurethane binder for abrasion resistance.
2. The protective coating system of claim 1, further comprising a water-borne acrylic dispersion with reduced solvent content.

title: Coating composition with hydrophobic topcoat
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a coating composition. claims: 1. A coating composition comprising: a fluorinated topcoat repelling water; a yttria-stabilised zirconia layer deposited by plasma spraying; and a diamond-like carbon film deposited by physical vapour deposition.

title: Corrosion protection scheme with sol-gel layer (continuation)
abstract: A corrosion protection scheme is disclosed that has a protective strip along the front edge made of tough elastomer adhesive tape guarding against droplet impact. In certain embodiments the corrosion protection scheme further includes a lubricant-impregnated textured film reducing the bond strength of ice and a soot-loaded polymer film that takes up solar radiation and warms. The arrangement lowers solvent emissions.
claims: 1. A corrosion protection scheme comprising: a protective strip along the front edge made of tough elastomer adhesive tape guarding against droplet impact; a lubricant-impregnated textured film reducing the bond strength of ice; and a soot-loaded polymer film that takes up solar radiation and warms.
2. The corrosion protection scheme of claim 1, further comprising a detector observing the frequency change of an oscillating probe to see accumulation of ice.
3. The corrosion protection scheme of claim 2, further comprising a resistive heater film buried under the finish and driven by a control unit.

title: Condition monitoring device with pressure transmitter and fibre sensing
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a condition monitoring device. The condition monitoring device comprises a diaphragm pressure transmitter with a current loop output and a fibre Bragg grating strain sensor bonded to the structure. Additionally, an intrinsically safe barrier limiting energy delivered to a hazardous area is provided. This shortens fault detection latency.
claims: 1. A condition monitoring device comprising: a diaphragm pressure transmitter with a current loop output; a fibre Bragg grating strain sensor bonded to the structure; and an intrinsically safe barrier limiting energy delivered to a hazardous area.
2. The condition monitoring device of claim 1, further comprising a calibration routine storing correction coefficients in non-volatile memory.
3. The condition monitoring device of claim 2, further comprising an inductive proximity sensor detecting a rotating target.

title: Laser melting machine with pore closing
abstract: A laser melting machine is disclosed that includes a batch record that links every part to the powder lot and the number of reuse cycles. In some embodiments the laser melting machine further includes a closed vessel carrying material in an inert atmosphere avoiding contact with ambient air and a scattering instrument determining grain size spread of reclaimed material. The arrangement lowers scrap rate.
claims: 1. A laser melting machine comprising: a batch record that links every part to the powder lot and the number of reuse cycles; a closed vessel carrying material in an inert atmosphere avoiding contact with ambient air; and a scattering instrument determining grain size spread of reclaimed material.
2. The laser melting machine of claim 1, further comprising a blending station that mixes used powder with virgin powder at a ratio selected from the measured properties.
3. The laser melting machine of claim 2, further comprising a flow assessment timing the outflow through a calibrated funnel.
4. The laser melting machine of claim 3, further comprising hot isostatic pressing to close internal pores.

title: Condition monitoring device with gas detection
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a condition monitoring device. The condition monitoring device comprises a micromachined acceleration transducer whose sampling frequency is raised upon larger oscillation levels and correcting sensor offset drift with readings from a nearby thermal resistor. Additionally, local spectrum analysis followed by a learned model scoring deviation from normal behaviour at the node is provided. This reduces maintenance visits.
claims: 1. A condition monitoring device comprising: a micromachined acceleration transducer whose sampling frequency is raised upon larger oscillation levels; correcting sensor offset drift with readings from a nearby thermal resistor; and local spectrum analysis followed by a learned model scoring deviation from normal behaviour at the node.
2. The condition monitoring device of claim 1, further comprising a calibration routine storing correction coefficients in non-volatile memory.
3. The condition monitoring device of claim 2, further comprising an intrinsically safe barrier limiting energy delivered to a hazardous area.
4. The condition monitoring device of claim 3, further comprising an electrochemical gas detection cell with a replaceable filter.

claims: 1. A additive manufacturing apparatus comprising: an orientation planner minimising overhang area; a post-build stress-relief heat treatment; and lattice support structures designed for easy removal.

2. The sensor node of claim 1, further comprising a piezoelectric energy harvester that powers the sensor node from machine vibration.
3. The sensor node of claim 2, further comprising a common clock reference aligning sample times between distributed nodes.
4. The sensor node of claim 3, further comprising an intrinsically safe barrier limiting energy delivered to a hazardous area.

A energy storage assembly comprising: a phase-change material layer disposed between adjacent battery cells to absorb heat; a controller that adjusts coolant flow rate using a predictive model of the cell temperature gradient; and an expanding fire-retardant layer together with an exhaust duct guiding vented gases out of the housing.
2. The energy storage assembly of claim 1, further comprising a cooling plate having serpentine microchannels through which coolant circulates.
3. The energy storage assembly of claim 2, further comprising a reversible heat pump that pre-heats the battery pack in cold ambient conditions.
4. The energy storage assembly of claim 3, further comprising a charging profile that derates current as cell temperature increases.

title: Sensor node with thermocouple assembly and long-range gateway
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sensor node. The sensor node comprises a light-sensing arc detector commanding a rapid breaker trip and a mineral-insulated thermocouple with a thermowell. Additionally, a gateway aggregating readings from field devices over a long-range radio link is provided. This lowers installation cost.
claims: 1. A sensor node comprising: a light-sensing arc detector commanding a rapid breaker trip; a mineral-insulated thermocouple with a thermowell; and a gateway aggregating readings from field devices over a long-range radio link.
2. The sensor node of claim 1, further comprising an unpowered acoustic-wave label at each conductor junction conveying heat readings.
3. The sensor node of claim 2, further comprising a reader aerial within the enclosure polling the transponders periodically.
4. The sensor node of claim 3, further comprising an ultrasonic transducer pair measuring transit time through the pipe wall.

title: Condition monitoring device with humidity compensation
abstract: A condition monitoring device is disclosed that includes a baseline of normal temperature rise as a function of load current learned during commissioning. In some embodiments the condition monitoring device further includes an alert issued when the temperature exceeds the baseline by a margin for a dwell time and a batteryless SAW transponder on every bar connection returning its temperature wirelessly. The arrangement extends battery life.
claims: 1. A condition monitoring device comprising: a baseline of normal temperature rise as a function of load current learned during commissioning; an alert issued when the temperature exceeds the baseline by a margin for a dwell time; and a batteryless SAW transponder on every bar connection returning its temperature wirelessly.
2. The condition monitoring device of claim 1, further comprising a viewing port of IR-transmitting glass built into the panel front.
3. The condition monitoring device of claim 2, further comprising a reader aerial within the enclosure polling the transponders periodically.
4. The condition monitoring device of claim 3, further comprising a humidity compensation step applied to capacitive readings.

title: Powder bed fusion system with multi-laser zoning
abstract: Embodiments of a powder bed fusion system are described, characterised by a controller that modifies the wire feed speed to keep the next layer height at a target. Variants include a pyrometer ensuring the workpiece cools beneath a bound prior to the next deposit. The design lowers scrap rate while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A powder bed fusion system comprising: a controller that modifies the wire feed speed to keep the next layer height at a target; a following inert gas shoe guarding the solidifying track against oxygen; and a pyrometer ensuring the workpiece cools beneath a bound prior to the next deposit.
2. The powder bed fusion system of claim 1, further comprising a structured light profilometer measuring the track elevation upon completion of every pass.
3. The powder bed fusion system of claim 2, further comprising a robot path generated from sliced geometry with continuous spiral tool paths avoiding arc restarts.
4. The powder bed fusion system of claim 3, further comprising a plurality of lasers each assigned to a zone of the build plate.

title: Machine health sensor with level radar
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a machine health sensor. The machine health sensor comprises a descriptor merging effective load level with energy in frequency bands for every pass and a fitted predictor returning the width of flank wear in microns. Additionally, an acoustic emission sensor attached to the tool holder detecting high-frequency bursts is provided. This lowers installation cost.
claims: 1. A machine health sensor comprising: a descriptor merging effective load level with energy in frequency bands for every pass; a fitted predictor returning the width of flank wear in microns; and an acoustic emission sensor attached to the tool holder detecting high-frequency bursts.
2. The machine health sensor of claim 1, further comprising a link to the machine controller ordering a replacement of the cutter once the estimate hits a bound.
3. The machine health sensor of claim 2, further comprising a virtual replica of machining tuned on the initial part of a lot.
4. The machine health sensor of claim 3, further comprising a guided-wave radar probe for tank level measurement.

title: Additive manufacturing apparatus with stress relief and graded lattice
abstract: A additive manufacturing apparatus is disclosed that includes a coaxial camera used only for recording build documentation. In some embodiments the additive manufacturing apparatus further includes a post-build stress-relief heat treatment and a topology-optimised lattice with graded cell size. The arrangement shortens qualification time.
claims: 1. A additive manufacturing apparatus comprising: a coaxial camera used only for recording build documentation; a post-build stress-relief heat treatment; and a topology-optimised lattice with graded cell size.
2. The additive manufacturing apparatus of claim 1, further comprising hot isostatic pressing to close internal pores.

title: Battery pack with heat spreader foils
abstract: Embodiments of a battery pack are described, characterised by an expanding fire-retardant layer together with an exhaust duct guiding vented gases out of the housing. Variants include a monitoring circuit flagging a cell failure event upon a temperature slope above a limit. The design improves fast-charging performance while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A battery pack comprising: an expanding fire-retardant layer together with an exhaust duct guiding vented gases out of the housing; a paraffin composite interposed between neighbouring cells, the composite storing latent heat during melting; and a monitoring circuit flagging a cell failure event upon a temperature slope above a limit.
2. The battery pack of claim 1, further comprising a cold plate with meandering micro-channels carrying liquid coolant beneath the cells.
3. The battery pack of claim 2, further comprising a control unit setting pump speed from a forecast of temperature differences across the cells.
4. The battery pack of claim 3, further comprising an aluminium heat-spreading foil wrapped around each cylindrical cell.

title: Powder bed fusion system with support structures and roller spreading
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a powder bed fusion system. The powder bed fusion system comprises lattice support structures designed for easy removal and a counter-rotating roller spreading powder. Additionally, a post-build stress-relief heat treatment is provided. This shortens qualification time.
claims: 1. A powder bed fusion system comprising: lattice support structures designed for easy removal; a counter-rotating roller spreading powder; and a post-build stress-relief heat treatment.
2. The powder bed fusion system of claim 1, further comprising an orientation planner minimising overhang area.
3. The powder bed fusion system of claim 2, further comprising a topology-optimised lattice with graded cell size.

title: Powder bed fusion system with surface finishing
abstract: A powder bed fusion system is disclosed that includes a post-processing machining step removing all dross. In some embodiments the powder bed fusion system further includes an abrasive flow process polishing internal channels and a data matrix mark printed on each part for traceability. The arrangement improves build yield.
claims: 1. A powder bed fusion system comprising: a post-processing machining step removing all dross; an abrasive flow process polishing internal channels; and a data matrix mark printed on each part for traceability.
2. The powder bed fusion system of claim 1, further comprising an orientation planner minimising overhang area.

title: Wireless monitoring system with scheduled logger
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a wireless monitoring system. The wireless monitoring system comprises a battery-powered data logger with scheduled wake-up and a fibre Bragg grating strain sensor bonded to the structure. Additionally, a humidity compensation step applied to capacitive readings is provided. This lowers installation cost.
claims: 1. A wireless monitoring system comprising: a battery-powered data logger with scheduled wake-up; a fibre Bragg grating strain sensor bonded to the structure; and a humidity compensation step applied to capacitive readings.
2. The wireless monitoring system of claim 1, further comprising a gateway aggregating readings from field devices over a long-range radio link.

title: Battery pack with air-cooled housing and heating film
abstract: Embodiments of a battery pack are described, characterised by a module housing with forced-air cooling ducts between cell rows. Variants include a dielectric fluid in which the cells are partially immersed. The design extends cycle life while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A battery pack comprising: a module housing with forced-air cooling ducts between cell rows; a resistive heating film attached to the pack underside; and a dielectric fluid in which the cells are partially immersed.
2. The battery pack of claim 1, further comprising a fan whose duty cycle follows the highest measured cell temperature.

title: Additive manufacturing apparatus with orientation planning
abstract: Embodiments of a additive manufacturing apparatus are described, characterised by an orientation planner minimising overhang area. Variants include a thermal distortion simulation used to pre-compensate part geometry. The design improves build yield while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A additive manufacturing apparatus comprising: an orientation planner minimising overhang area; a plurality of lasers each assigned to a zone of the build plate; and a thermal distortion simulation used to pre-compensate part geometry.
2. The additive manufacturing apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a sieving station returning unfused powder to the hopper.

title: Thermal management system with heating film and heat pipe
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a thermal management system. The thermal management system comprises a resistive heating film attached to the pack underside and a heat pipe transferring heat from the module core to a condenser section. Additionally, a plurality of thermistors bonded to cell surfaces is provided. This improves fast-charging performance.
claims: 1. A thermal management system comprising: a resistive heating film attached to the pack underside; a heat pipe transferring heat from the module core to a condenser section; and a plurality of thermistors bonded to cell surfaces.
2. The thermal management system of claim 1, further comprising a module housing with forced-air cooling ducts between cell rows.

title: Additive manufacturing apparatus with wire deposition
abstract: Embodiments of a additive manufacturing apparatus are described, characterised by a geometry analyser that classifies downward-facing surfaces by overhang angle. Variants include a chessboard sector exposure with square cells of 5 mm. The design reduces porosity in finished parts while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A additive manufacturing apparatus comprising: a geometry analyser that classifies downward-facing surfaces by overhang angle; a slender breakaway rib taken off with an electrical discharge wire; and a chessboard sector exposure with square cells of 5 mm.
2. The additive manufacturing apparatus of claim 1, further comprising an infrared imager spotting hot spots under protruding regions and marking the slice.
3. The additive manufacturing apparatus of claim 2, further comprising a machine learning model trained on past builds that predicts dross formation from the scan parameters.
4. The additive manufacturing apparatus of claim 3, further comprising a wire-fed arc deposition head mounted on a robot arm.

title: Sensor node with thermocouple assembly
abstract: A sensor node is disclosed that includes a manual tool inspection by microscope after each shift. In some embodiments the sensor node further includes a mineral-insulated thermocouple with a thermowell and a battery-powered data logger with scheduled wake-up. The arrangement shortens fault detection latency.
claims: 1. A sensor node comprising: a manual tool inspection by microscope after each shift; a mineral-insulated thermocouple with a thermowell; and a battery-powered data logger with scheduled wake-up.
2. The sensor node of claim 1, further comprising a self-diagnostic function reporting sensor element failure.

title: Battery pack with aerogel cover and cell balancing
abstract: A battery pack is disclosed that includes an aerogel insulation blanket covering the pack lid. In some embodiments the battery pack further includes a balancing circuit that equalises the state of charge of series-connected cells and a heat pipe transferring heat from the module core to a condenser section. The arrangement extends cycle life.
claims: 1. A battery pack comprising: an aerogel insulation blanket covering the pack lid; a balancing circuit that equalises the state of charge of series-connected cells; and a heat pipe transferring heat from the module core to a condenser section.
2. The battery pack of claim 1, further comprising an aluminium heat-spreading foil wrapped around each cylindrical cell.

title: Thermal management system with heating film and sealed enclosure
abstract: Embodiments of a thermal management system are described, characterised by an aerogel insulation blanket covering the pack lid. Variants include a sealed pack enclosure with a pressure-equalising membrane. The design lowers parasitic cooling power while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A thermal management system comprising: an aerogel insulation blanket covering the pack lid; a bidirectional refrigerant circuit warming the pack before charging at low temperature; and a sealed pack enclosure with a pressure-equalising membrane.
2. The thermal management system of claim 1, further comprising a processor regulating coolant throughput according to a model predicting thermal gradients between cells.
3. The thermal management system of claim 2, further comprising a resistive heating film attached to the pack underside.
4. The thermal management system of claim 3, further comprising an expanding fire-retardant layer together with an exhaust duct guiding vented gases out of the housing.

title: Additive manufacturing apparatus with support structures and orientation planning
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a additive manufacturing apparatus. The additive manufacturing apparatus comprises lattice support structures designed for easy removal and a post-build stress-relief heat treatment. Additionally, a drag-along argon cup shielding the cooling weld from air is provided. This reduces porosity in finished parts.
claims: 1. A additive manufacturing apparatus comprising: lattice support structures designed for easy removal; a post-build stress-relief heat treatment; and a drag-along argon cup shielding the cooling weld from air.
2. The additive manufacturing apparatus of claim 1, further comprising an orientation planner minimising overhang area.
3. The additive manufacturing apparatus of claim 2, further comprising a pressing cylinder working the fresh track before it cools.

title: Machine health sensor with safety barrier
abstract: Embodiments of a machine health sensor are described, characterised by a numerical control interface that triggers a tool change when the wear estimate reaches a limit. Variants include a current transformer around a drive conductor logging the electric load of the cutting spindle. The design reduces maintenance visits while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A machine health sensor comprising: a numerical control interface that triggers a tool change when the wear estimate reaches a limit; a virtual replica of machining tuned on the initial part of a lot; and a current transformer around a drive conductor logging the electric load of the cutting spindle.
2. The machine health sensor of claim 1, further comprising a regression model that outputs flank wear width in micrometres.
3. The machine health sensor of claim 2, further comprising a piezo ultrasonic pickup on the toolholder sensing high frequency events.
4. The machine health sensor of claim 3, further comprising an intrinsically safe barrier limiting energy delivered to a hazardous area.

title: Protective coating system with low-solvent binder and abrasion resistance
abstract: Embodiments of a protective coating system are described, characterised by ceramic particles dispersed in a polyurethane binder for abrasion resistance. Variants include a buried electrically heated layer supplied by a regulator. The design reduces maintenance repainting while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A protective coating system comprising: ceramic particles dispersed in a polyurethane binder for abrasion resistance; a fluorinated topcoat repelling water; and a buried electrically heated layer supplied by a regulator.
2. The protective coating system of claim 1, further comprising a pigmented elastomer sheet turning sunshine into thermal energy.
3. The protective coating system of claim 2, further comprising a water-borne acrylic dispersion with reduced solvent content.
4. The protective coating system of claim 3, further comprising a sacrificial edge guard of polymer tape resisting raindrop wear.

title: Layer-wise fabrication method with wire deposition (continuation)
abstract: Embodiments of a layer-wise fabrication method are described, characterised by an on-axis optical detector sensing radiation from the molten pool via the scanning optics. Variants include a shielding gas stream monitored by an oxygen analyser and a spatter deflector. The design lowers porosity in finished parts while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A layer-wise fabrication method comprising: an on-axis optical detector sensing radiation from the molten pool via the scanning optics; closed-loop regulation of beam power per scan segment according to sensed melt data; and a shielding gas stream monitored by an oxygen analyser and a spatter deflector.
2. The layer-wise fabrication method of claim 1, further comprising a linear optical scanner carried by the spreader inspecting the powder bed for defects.
3. The layer-wise fabrication method of claim 2, further comprising a fast infrared imager from which the molten track width is computed.

title: Coated article with anti-fouling paint
abstract: Embodiments of a coated article are described, characterised by a calorimetric verification demanding forty per cent lower peak heat release. Variants include exfoliating graphite platelets boosting the swelling factor. The design improves adhesion on steel while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A coated article comprising: a calorimetric verification demanding forty per cent lower peak heat release; a crustacean-derived polysaccharide acting as a charring agent expanding into a cellular layer; and exfoliating graphite platelets boosting the swelling factor.
2. The coated article of claim 1, further comprising a phytic acid phosphorus source derived from rice bran.
3. The coated article of claim 2, further comprising a waterborne acrylic binder with less than fifty grams per litre of volatile organic compounds.
4. The coated article of claim 3, further comprising a copper-free anti-fouling paint releasing a biocide slowly.

title: Protective coating system with powder coating (continuation)
abstract: Embodiments of a protective coating system are described, characterised by a cone calorimeter acceptance test requiring a peak heat release rate reduction of forty percent. Variants include a crustacean-derived polysaccharide acting as a charring agent expanding into a cellular layer. The design reduces maintenance repainting while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A protective coating system comprising: a cone calorimeter acceptance test requiring a peak heat release rate reduction of forty percent; exfoliating graphite platelets boosting the swelling factor; and a crustacean-derived polysaccharide acting as a charring agent expanding into a cellular layer.
2. The protective coating system of claim 1, further comprising a clear topcoat of polyurethane protecting the intumescent layer from moisture.
3. The protective coating system of claim 2, further comprising a phosphorus compound obtained from grain husk phytate.

title: Additive manufacturing apparatus with graded lattice and scan strategy
abstract: Embodiments of a additive manufacturing apparatus are described, characterised by a topology-optimised lattice with graded cell size. Variants include hot isostatic pressing to close internal pores. The design reduces porosity in finished parts while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A additive manufacturing apparatus comprising: a topology-optimised lattice with graded cell size; a stripe scan strategy rotated by sixty-seven degrees between layers; and hot isostatic pressing to close internal pores.
2. The additive manufacturing apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a post-build stress-relief heat treatment.

title: Coating composition with abrasion resistance
abstract: Embodiments of a coating composition are described, characterised by a bi-component epoxide undercoat with an amine curing agent spread over the blasted joint region. Variants include a wireless tag buried at the joint storing the application parameters and operator identity. The design lowers solvent emissions while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A coating composition comprising: a bi-component epoxide undercoat with an amine curing agent spread over the blasted joint region; a pull-off adhesion test recording the load in megapascals; and a wireless tag buried at the joint storing the application parameters and operator identity.
2. The coating composition of claim 1, further comprising a thermally contracting wrap with sticky sealant covering the circumferential weld.
3. The coating composition of claim 2, further comprising a spark tester using high voltage to reveal pinholes in the film.
4. The coating composition of claim 3, further comprising ceramic particles dispersed in a polyurethane binder for abrasion resistance.

title: Layer-wise fabrication method with powder recycling
abstract: A layer-wise fabrication method is disclosed that includes a sieving station returning unfused powder to the hopper. In some embodiments the layer-wise fabrication method further includes hot isostatic pressing to close internal pores and a wire-fed arc deposition head mounted on a robot arm. The arrangement shortens qualification time.
claims: 1. A layer-wise fabrication method comprising: a sieving station returning unfused powder to the hopper; hot isostatic pressing to close internal pores; and a wire-fed arc deposition head mounted on a robot arm.

title: Layer-wise fabrication method with pore closing and part marking
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a layer-wise fabrication method. The layer-wise fabrication method comprises hot isostatic pressing to close internal pores and a data matrix mark printed on each part for traceability. Additionally, a plurality of lasers each assigned to a zone of the build plate is provided. This improves build yield.
claims: 1. A layer-wise fabrication method comprising: hot isostatic pressing to close internal pores; a data matrix mark printed on each part for traceability; and a plurality of lasers each assigned to a zone of the build plate.

title: Sensor node with fibre sensing and long-range gateway
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a sensor node. The sensor node comprises a force dynamometer used in laboratory cutting trials and a fibre Bragg grating strain sensor bonded to the structure. Additionally, a gateway aggregating readings from field devices over a long-range radio link is provided. This shortens fault detection latency.
claims: 1. A sensor node comprising: a force dynamometer used in laboratory cutting trials; a fibre Bragg grating strain sensor bonded to the structure; and a gateway aggregating readings from field devices over a long-range radio link.
2. The sensor node of claim 1, further comprising a mineral-insulated thermocouple with a thermowell.

title: Sensor node with fibre sensing
abstract: Embodiments of a sensor node are described, characterised by a fibre Bragg grating strain sensor bonded to the structure. Variants include an inductive proximity sensor detecting a rotating target. The design extends battery life while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A sensor node comprising: a fibre Bragg grating strain sensor bonded to the structure; a guided-wave radar probe for tank level measurement; and an inductive proximity sensor detecting a rotating target.
2. The sensor node of claim 1, further comprising a diaphragm pressure transmitter with a current loop output.

title: Coated article with thermal barrier
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a coated article. The coated article comprises a yttria-stabilised zirconia layer deposited by plasma spraying and a water-borne acrylic dispersion with reduced solvent content. Additionally, a sealed anodic oxide layer on an aluminium alloy is provided. This improves adhesion on steel.
claims: 1. A coated article comprising: a yttria-stabilised zirconia layer deposited by plasma spraying; a water-borne acrylic dispersion with reduced solvent content; and a sealed anodic oxide layer on an aluminium alloy.

title: Battery module with heat spreader foils
abstract: Embodiments of a battery module are described, characterised by a new-cell production line with end-of-line capacity grading. Variants include a fan whose duty cycle follows the highest measured cell temperature. The design extends cycle life while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A battery module comprising: a new-cell production line with end-of-line capacity grading; an aluminium heat-spreading foil wrapped around each cylindrical cell; and a fan whose duty cycle follows the highest measured cell temperature.
2. The battery module of claim 1, further comprising a resistive heating film attached to the pack underside.

title: Thermal management system with immersion cooling
abstract: Embodiments of a thermal management system are described, characterised by an insulated pack lid with aerogel panels reducing heat loss in parked vehicles. Variants include a warm-up timetable matched to the route target and planned departure. The design extends cycle life while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A thermal management system comprising: an insulated pack lid with aerogel panels reducing heat loss in parked vehicles; a resistive metal sheet inside the electrode assembly warmed by the battery's discharge current; and a warm-up timetable matched to the route target and planned departure.
2. The thermal management system of claim 1, further comprising a lithium plating detector that analyses the voltage plateau during relaxation after charging.
3. The thermal management system of claim 2, further comprising a lookup-based amperage ceiling that varies with cell temperature held in controller memory.
4. The thermal management system of claim 3, further comprising a dielectric fluid in which the cells are partially immersed.

title: Battery pack with fan control (continuation)
abstract: A battery pack is described that includes a fan whose duty cycle follows the highest measured cell temperature. In certain embodiments the battery pack further includes a compressible thermal interface pad between the cell and a cooling surface and a module housing with forced-air cooling ducts between cell rows. The arrangement lowers temperature spread between cells.
claims: 1. A battery pack comprising: a fan whose duty cycle follows the highest measured cell temperature; a compressible thermal interface pad between the cell and a cooling surface; and a module housing with forced-air cooling ducts between cell rows.
2. The battery pack of claim 1, further comprising a dielectric fluid in which the cells are partially immersed.

title: Thermal management system with thermistor network
abstract: Embodiments of a thermal management system are described, characterised by a charge schedule lowering the amperage upon expansion speed above a bound. Variants include a pressing plate with a motorised clamp load regulated in response to sensed expansion. The design extends cycle life while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A thermal management system comprising: a charge schedule lowering the amperage upon expansion speed above a bound; a lumped electrical model deriving rising ohmic resistance from the response to current pulses; and a pressing plate with a motorised clamp load regulated in response to sensed expansion.
2. The thermal management system of claim 1, further comprising a resilient cushioning layer maintaining steady compressive contact throughout ageing.
3. The thermal management system of claim 2, further comprising an optical fibre gauge placed in the gap between neighbouring cells to sense cell expansion.
4. The thermal management system of claim 3, further comprising a plurality of thermistors bonded to cell surfaces.

title: Powder bed fusion system with pore closing and scan strategy
abstract: Embodiments of a powder bed fusion system are described, characterised by hot isostatic pressing to close internal pores. Variants include a topology-optimised lattice with graded cell size. The design improves build yield while keeping cost low.
claims: 1. A powder bed fusion system comprising: hot isostatic pressing to close internal pores; a stripe scan strategy rotated by sixty-seven degrees between layers; and a topology-optimised lattice with graded cell size.
2. The powder bed fusion system of claim 1, further comprising a counter-rotating roller spreading powder.
3. The powder bed fusion system of claim 2, further comprising a post-build stress-relief heat treatment.

title: Additive manufacturing apparatus with stress relief (continuation)
abstract: A additive manufacturing apparatus is described that has a flow assessment timing the outflow through a calibrated funnel. In certain embodiments the additive manufacturing apparatus further includes a gas-extraction analyser quantifying oxygen and nitrogen in the feedstock and a scattering instrument determining grain size spread of reclaimed material. The arrangement lowers scrap rate.
claims: 1. A additive manufacturing apparatus comprising: a flow assessment timing the outflow through a calibrated funnel; a gas-extraction analyser quantifying oxygen and nitrogen in the feedstock; and a scattering instrument determining grain size spread of reclaimed material.
2. The additive manufacturing apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a mixer combining reclaimed and fresh powder in a proportion chosen from measurements.
3. The additive manufacturing apparatus of claim 2, further comprising a ledger associating each component with its feedstock lot and recycling count.

title: Thermal management system with cell balancing
abstract: The present disclosure relates to a thermal management system. The thermal management system comprises a balancing circuit that equalises the state of charge of series-connected cells and a pyrolytic graphite sheet conducting heat toward a side wall. Additionally, an aerogel insulation blanket covering the pack lid is provided. This improves fast-charging performance.
claims: 1. A thermal management system comprising: a balancing circuit that equalises the state of charge of series-connected cells; a pyrolytic graphite sheet conducting heat toward a side wall; and an aerogel insulation blanket covering the pack lid.
2. The thermal management system of claim 1, further comprising a charging profile that derates current as cell temperature increases.
3. The thermal management system of claim 2, further comprising a busbar with an integrated heat sink.

title: Machine health sensor with safety barrier (continuation)
abstract: Embodiments of a machine health sensor are described, characterised by a numerical control interface that triggers a tool change when the wear estimate reaches a limit. Variants include a current transformer around a drive conductor logging the electric load of the cutting spindle. The design lowers maintenance visits while keeping cost low.

A machine health sensor comprising: a numerical control interface that triggers a tool change when the wear estimate reaches a limit; a virtual replica of machining tuned on the initial part of a lot; and a current transformer around a drive conductor logging the electric load of the cutting spindle.
2. The machine health sensor of claim 1, further comprising a regression model that outputs flank wear width in micrometres.
3. The machine health sensor of claim 2, further comprising a piezo ultrasonic pickup on the toolholder sensing high frequency events.
